sections.label: The story of your project this year

content.text: This section could not be drafted from the material available in uploaded documents or confirmed gap answers for the reporting period. No citable source in the uploaded documents or confirmed gap answers supplied material for "The story of your project this year". Accordingly, no narrative is presented here: the organisation has left this section blank rather than report anything not supported by the available evidence.

sections.label: How you involved people from your community

content.text:
We involved people from the community directly in shaping delivery. Residents co-designed three evening workshops in July 2026, which meant local people had a clear role in deciding how these sessions were run. We also kept attendance registers for those workshops, so we had a basic record of who took part.

We worked with Southbank Community Trust as a local partner. Together, we delivered a shared volunteer rota and joint outreach. This helped us involve community members not only through activities themselves, but also through the way delivery was organised with a local organisation.

claims.text: Residents co-designed three evening workshops in July 2026.
Attendance registers were kept for those workshops.
A partnership with Southbank Community Trust delivered a shared volunteer rota and joint outreach.

sections.label: The differences you are making, both big and small

content.text:
We reached 148 people through at least one hub session against a target of 120.

Of the 148 people reached, 42 were children aged 8–11, 39 were young people aged 12–16, 53 were adults aged 17–64, and 11 were older residents aged 65+.

Among those attending at least one hub session, 86 were female, 54 were male, and 5 were non-binary or preferred not to say.

97 people attending at least one hub session were recorded with a vulnerability or low-income flag.

61 children and young people attended at least three sessions against a target of 55.

sections.label: How you are changing what you do

content.text:
We changed how we worked by involving local people more directly in shaping activity and by working more closely with a local partner. Residents co-designed three evening workshops in July 2026 and kept attendance registers. This showed a more active role for the community in planning and tracking participation, rather than only attending activity.

We also worked in partnership with Southbank Community Trust to deliver a shared volunteer rota and joint outreach. In practice, this meant we adjusted delivery so that staffing and outreach were coordinated across organisations, which helped us organise work in a more joined-up way.

The project ran from 2025-05-01 to 2026-10-31, and these changes formed part of how delivery developed during the grant period. The submitted records did not include a clear statement of any further planned changes or any support needed, so we have not added detail beyond the evidence available.

conflicts.annotation: The monitoring/spend table states a total programme budget of £78,500, while the award letter states the approved grant is £82,000 — a £3,500 discrepancy. The delivery note in Table2!E17 explicitly acknowledges this gap ('award letter says £82k'). Possible explanations include: (a) the monitoring table budget was drawn up before the final award amount was confirmed; (b) the grantee has not updated the spend table to reflect the full award; or (c) a portion of the award (£3,500) is unallocated/held in reserve and not reflected in the line-item budget. Gate-1 reviewer should request clarification from the grantee on whether the full £82,000 award is accounted for.

conflicts.annotation: The monitoring/spend table states a total programme budget of £78,500, while the award letter states the approved grant is £82,000 — a £3,500 discrepancy. The delivery note in Table2!E17 explicitly acknowledges this gap ('award letter says £82k'). Possible explanations include: (a) the monitoring table budget was drawn up before the final award amount was confirmed; (b) the grantee has not updated the spend table to reflect the full award; or (c) a portion of the award (£3,500) is unallocated/held in reserve and not reflected in the line-item budget. Gate-1 reviewer should request clarification from the grantee on whether the full £82,000 award is accounted for.
